question: Question linked to image no. 2 In the case described above and regarding pharmacological treatment, which is the correct statement.

options.opa: The pharmacological treatment is not necessary since the bleeding lesion has been identified.
options.opb: The ideal treatment for this patient is perfusion of somatostatin since it is a hepatopathic patient.
options.opc: The use of omeprazole at high doses reduces the recurrence of bleeding.
options.opd: Ranitidine is the drug of choice to avoid pharmacological toxicity when dealing with a patient with chronic liver disease.
options.ope: The eradication of Helicobacter pylori is the first measure to be taken.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Bleeding lesion identified -> Pharmacological treatment may still be necessary -> 70% CHAIN: Hepatopathic patient -> Consider somatostatin perfusion -> 60% CHAIN: High-dose omeprazole -> Potential reduction in bleeding recurrence -> 50% CHAIN: Chronic liver disease -> Consider ranitidine to avoid pharmacological toxicity -> 60% CHAIN: Presence of Helicobacter pylori -> Eradication as the initial measure -> 70%
analysis: In the case of a bleeding lesion in a patient with chronic liver disease, the use of omeprazole at high doses is recommended to reduce the recurrence of bleeding by suppressing gastric acid secretion and promoting ulcer healing.
